name.baseName: Disposal, copper in car shredder residue, 0% water, to municipal incineration

dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: This dataset represents the activity of waste disposal of copper in car shredder residue in a municipal solid waste incinerator (MSWI) Recommended use of this dataset: For disposal of rather fine or dusty copper, which goes to incineration as part of Automotive Shredder Residue (ASR). Due to fine grain size of the particles, 50% burnability is assumed, therefore not suited for less fine copper parts in waste. Pure, isolated copper fractions will not be disposed in incinerators, but rather go to recycling. Inventoried waste contains 50% Cu in ASR burnable; 50% Cu in ASR inert; . Waste composition (wet, in ppm): H2O n.a.; O n.a.; H n.a.; C n.a.; S 0.0000028372; N n.a.; P n.a.; B n.a.; Cl n.a.; Br n.a.; F n.a.; I n.a.; Ag 489.05; As n.a.; Ba n.a.; Cd n.a.; Co n.a.; Cr 2.7346; Cu 924870; Hg n.a.; Mn 1483.2; Mo n.a.; Ni 4062.3; Pb 0.0044823; Sb 3438.1; Se n.a.; Sn 8733.9; V 0.00002178; Zn 1075.5; Be n.a.; Sc n.a.; Sr n.a.; Ti n.a.; Tl n.a.; W n.a.; Si 6428.2; Fe 9181.1; Ca n.a.; Al 40233; K n.a.; Mg n.a.; Na n.a.; Share of carbon in waste that is biogenic 60.4%. Share of metals in waste not oxidised and bulk-recyclable (exclude very small or thin parts) Iron: 0%; Alu: 0%; Copper: 50%. One kg of this waste produces 1.135 kg of slag and 0.07842 kg of residues, which are landfilled. Additional solidification with 0.03137 kg of cement. Net energy production: 0MJ/kg electric energy and 0MJ/kg thermal energy. Recovery of metal scrap to recycling: 0g iron scrap, 0g aluminium scrap, 135.4g copper scrap.; Formula: Cu;; UUID: 7c33eb3d-7fa7-4625-a791-6e4954400b3b

time.common:timeRepresentativenessDescription: Waste composition as given in literature reference, theoretical data or other source. Transfer coefficients for modern MSWI.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Specific to the technology mix encountered in Switzerland in 2010. Well applicable to modern incineration practices in Europe, North America or Japan.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
average Swiss MSWI plants in 2010 (grate incinerators) with electrostatic precipitator for fly ash (ESP), wet flue gas scrubber and 25% SNCR , 42.77% SCR-high dust , 32.68% SCR-low dust -DeNOx facilities and 0% without Denox (weighted according to mass of burnt waste, representing Swiss average). Efficiency of iron scrap separation from slag : 58%. Efficiency of non-ferrous scrap separation from slag : 31%. Gross electric efficiency technology mix 15.84% and Gross thermal efficiency technology mix 28.51%

# Included processes
Waste incineration from waste reception gate further downstream (excluding transport to the MSWI plant). Waste-specific air and water emisions from incineration, auxiliary material consumption for flue gas cleaning. Short-term emissions to river water and long-term emisisons to ground water from slag compartment (from bottom ash) and residual material landfill (from solidified fly ashes and scrubber slugde). Waste-specific process energy demands for MSWI and net energy generation.
